newsitem.title: USA: Disabled activists back Clinton over Dole.
newsitem.headline: Disabled activists back Clinton over Dole.

text.p: Several activists for the disabled, including a life-long Republican who serves on the Dole Foundation, on Wednesday endorsed President Bill Clinton over Republican Bob Dole, himself disabled by a war injury.

Justin Dart, a Republican who is on the board of the foundation that Dole founded to help the disabled, said Dole had done his fellow disabled people a disservice by backing House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich's agenda.
Dart, wheelchair-bound since 1948 because of polio, was an early backer of Ronald Reagan and worked on disability issues for him and George Bush when they were president.

Dart said he had personally helped pay for the wheelchair ramp outside the Republicans' national headquarters. But he said the policies favoured by Republican congressional leaders on health, education, housing, nursing homes and welfare were harmful to disabled people.
"I love the man," Dart said of Dole, whom he had supported for years. "But I love the American dream more ... In 1996 I am a Republican for Clinton."

Dole was badly injured as a young soldier in the Second World War and has permanent damage to his right hand, arm and shoulder. He has difficulty with many simple tasks such as cutting meat on a dinner plate or putting on a coat.

Dole has been a long-time supporter of the Americans with Disabilities Act, but Dart and several other activists, some of whom have had high profiles in fighting for disability legislation or health reform, faulted him at a news conference for endorsing the policies of Gingrich, which they called the "tragic politics of retreat."
A Dole spokesman was not immediately available for comment but the campaign has often cited Dole's record of legislation aiding the disabled.
